correctness.rationale: Exact finite law follows from exhaustive two-round conditioning and symmetric gambler’s ruin on the two surviving players. The transform satisfies the classical difference boundary problem and mean follows from a(N-a); every boundary k=0,1,m is treated. Dense limit uses a scaled hyperbolic-cosine transform. Sparse limit uses the full killed-chain sine expansion, with uniform Gaussian domination and negative-mode estimates, plus a reflection-principle concentration bound. The included independent original-chain rational checker passed 2,205 assertions.

originality.rationale: The original paper defines the precise model and in Remark 3.4 qualitatively reduces its one/two-card initial states to two-player ruin and predicts mk-order expected time. Those are credited prior ingredients. The proposed exact full finite distribution and PGF, all-positive-density diffusion law, and rare m²-time theta profile are not stated in the inspected relevant complete paper, nor obtained from its published bounds without the present conditional probabilities and spectral asymptotics. The two-player paper only covers the already known ruin ingredient. Targeted published-finding corpus searches returned no equivalent or stronger absorption result. Residual historical-priority risk persists.
residual_risks: No exhaustive historical-priority guarantee; general gambler’s-ruin entrance-law literature may give equivalent specializations under different terminology.
Original Remark 3.4 gives the core two-step reduction and approximate mk mean, so that qualitative mechanism alone is not novel.
Brownian exit-time and killed-chain spectral methods are classical; claimed contribution is their exact identification and rare asymptotic in this specific model.

value.rationale: Remark 3.4 of the motivating paper singles out exactly this one/two-card near-critical regime and only describes a rough duration transition. The complete law quantifies every m and k, and the sparse regime proves a surprising discrepancy between typical time and its mean with a sharp theta-series probability profile. These precise quantities are natural observables of a well-motivated stochastic model and enable further finite and asymptotic analysis.
